John Tonry 5/12/88
Implemented in xvista with various mods - J. Holtzman 5/90-5/91, 96

Extracted into standalone version and added doxygen markup

2005 May 27

void imagemap (  float  zero,
float  span,
int  ncolors
) 
 

Create the color loolup table.

Parameters:
zero zero point (min) of the intensity mapping
span span of the intensity mapping (max-min)
ncolors Number of colors to map
Creates the global breakpts array that is used to quickly map image data values into display colors. The breakpts array contains those data values that map into each "color" index in the palette vector.

The mapping is: 

  breakpt[i] = zero + (span/(ncolors-2)) * i
Note that this algorithm reserves the top 2 colors in the palette for non-data uses.

void imagedraw (  int  xuser,
int  yuser,
int  color
) 
 

Draw to user coordinates (X,Y) from the last position.

Parameters:
xuser X-axis coordinate in user space
yuser Y-axis coordinate in user space
color color to use (from the palette)
Draws a line from the last vector position (previous imagerelocate() or imagedraw() call) to the given (X,Y) location with a particular palette color.

The line will not appear immediately on the overlay plane unless the display is refreshed.

See also:
imagerelocate(), imagedrawflush()

void lights (  int  state  ) 
 

Work the various status "lights" on the display.

Parameters:
state status light to operate and its state: +=on/-=off
The display status lights are numbered 1..4 running from top to bottom. In order: 
  Light 1: Input State (-1=Asychronous, +1=waiting for key press)
  Light 2: Image State (-2=no image, 2=image loaded & ready)
  Light 3: Zoom Window State (-3=frozen, +3=active)
  Light 4: Image Zoom State (-4 = normal, +4=zoomed in/out)
In the normal state the light is green, otherwise it is red.

If state=0, it turns all the lights on GREEN (+state)

void imagelight (  int  upper,
char *  mess,
int  color
) 
 

Draw an status light on the display.

Parameters:
upper tells which light to draw in (see below)
mess String to be written (null terminated)
color 0/1 for red/green
Draws a status light. The values of upper give which light is to be operated: 
  upper = -1 -> redraw all
  upper = 1  -> top light
  upper = 2  -> next from top
  upper = 3  -> next from bottom
  upper = 4  -> bottom light
Or, graphically 
  +-------+
  |   1   |
  +-------+
  |   2   |
  +-------+
  |   3   |
  +-------+
  |   4   |
  +-------+

int imageread (  int *  x,
int *  y,
char *  key
) 
 

Blocking read from the display of one character.

Parameters:
x User X-axis coordinate where the key was struck
y User Y-axis coordinate where the key was struck
key ASCII code of the key struck
Puts the cursor on the image and waits for a key to be hit (used, e.g., to prompt for user cursor interaction on the image).

Blocking is rude, so do it sparingly.

void updatename (  char *  text,
int  num
) 
 

update the name that appears on the image display

Parameters:
text string with the new image name
num number of the text string to change (1 or 2)
Changes one or other of the label strings for the xyz status subwindow (displays cursor x,y and corresponding data values). 
  num=1 sets imname1[], the top label
  num=2 sets imname2[], the middle label
Any other values of num are ignored.

Note that the bottom label in the xzy subwindow is either the position/data readout if the cursor is on the image, or the color lookup table value if the cursor is on the color palette subwindow.

Repacks the color palette (compresses it) to have the effect of changing the image intensity scaling (zeropoint and span), though at a sacrifice of bit depth, by re-mapping the intensities to only span palette indexes n1..n2 (normally it runs 0..npalette-1).

float *  breakpts,

) 
 

Map floating image data into integer display data.

Parameters:
x0 X-axis coordinate of origin of image section to map
y0 Y-axis coordinate of origin of image section to map
nx X-axis size of image section to map
ny Y-axis size of image section to map
datw Number of data pixels per row in full image
data array of data to be mapped
imx0 X-axis origin of the image array
imy0 Y-axis origin of the image array
imw Number of image pixels per row
yinv Flag: invert y order of data and image
image array to receive mapped data
breakpts lookup table
nbreak fallback branch table for ambiguous cases
pixels color cells vector (defined in zimage.h)
bits_per_pixel data precision (bits per pixel), values: 8, 16, or 24
cmask color mask
Uses the lookup table to map image data values into N-bit display values for display. Unlike an older version of mapimage(), this version knows about multiple color planes and color masks (e.g., for RGB color planes in a TrueColor visual like a 24-bit display device).
